But at m9 (all cores max) ALL sensors 5-9% high; at nominal ~6%. Excess only appears with MULTIPLE hot cores => MUTUAL/lateral coupling under-modeled, OR global rise error that averages out in noisy singles. Two rival hypotheses: (H_couple) lateral core-core edges too weak; (H_global) global rise underestimated ~6% (R-to-ambient or power), hidden in noisy singles. Decisive test: m9 has 8 hot cores, huge mutual term. H_global predicts uniform % across all incl pkg. H_couple predicts localized pattern. Reverted bad v_core4 edit. ONLY real: core4. m4 (c4 max): c4self+0.71,c6+1.38,c7+1.02,c0+0.77; c1-0.69,c3-0.65,pkg-0.85 m5 (c6 max): c6+0.85,c1+1.16,c3+1.08,c4+0.33 m7 (c7 max): c7self-0.60, c4+1.23,c6+0.75 m8 (c0 max): c0self+0.57,c4+0.40,c3-1.28,pkg-2.08 m11 (c2 max): c2self-1.28,c4+0.63,c5+1.08,c7+1.00,pkg-1.00 m12 (c5 max): c5+0.55,c4+1.21,pkg-1.61 m15 (c1 max): c1self+0.13,c4+1.55 m9 (all max): all +1.4..+5.2, pkg+2.23, core4 worst +5.15 KEY FACTS: - SELF-heating residual ~0 for all cores (diagonal correct). +/-1 = quant+noise. - core4 residual POSITIVE in every scenario, magnitude grows with total die heat and with neighbor heat. NOT f(core4 own temp): at t55 residuals span 0.4-1.55. So NOT a core4 sensor fault -> MODEL coupling into core4 under-predicted. - Package residual ~0 at m1/m6, +2.23 only at m9 (near power cap 95W). Package = total heat gauge -> total heat removal CORRECT; it's DISTRIBUTION that's wrong. - CONFLICT: at m1 core4 needs to be model-HOTTER (own heat context); at m6 core4 needs model-HOTTER (periphery heat context, core4 own power min). A single lateral/vertical coupling edge cannot do both (opposite coupling-sign requirements). => likely raising core4's heat-LOSS resistance (b_core4, boundary) which scales with total flux through core4 region regardless of source. 279NoteBREAKTHROUGH - core4 residual vs TOTAL die power: m2(min,8W): +0.34 | m4(20W):+0.71 | m12(20W):+1.21 | m6(periph41W,c4cold):+2.28 | m1(nom80W):+4.39 | m9(allmax95W):+5.15 resid/totalpower: 0.043,0.036,0.061,0.055,0.055,0.054 => ~0.05 C/W CONSTANT for mid/high power. => core4 model error ~= 0.05 * TOTAL die power. core4 under-predicts core4 temp by heat proportional to WHOLE-die power. Mechanism candidate: core4 silicon couples too WEAKLY to the shared IHS (v_core4 too HIGH=too insulating in model). IHS is the heat-spreading node whose temp rises with total power. If real v_core4 LOWER (more conductive), core4 tracks hot IHS: hotter at m6(periph hot),m1,m9 (IHS hot); at m4 core4 is the source so effect small (self ok). This explains ALL signs incl m6 (periph hot,IHS hot, core4 cold power yet reads hot). TEST: LOWER v_core4. (Earlier I only tested RAISE which overshot.) Also note: at m1 cores 0,5,6,7 also +2-3 (∝ total power), c2,c3 near 0. So maybe not only core4 - a broader IHS-tracking weakness. But core4 strongest.

536Prune h1Halving all core-core lateral R (doubling conductance) made m1 cores colder (c4 model 89.45 vs pristine 91.61), moving away from the measured-hotter reality. If lateral coupling were too weak, more conductance would help; it hurts. Core4 is not under-coupled laterally.
537Prune h3Same lateral test refutes IHS-lateral core4 under-coupling: increasing lihs conductance cooled core4 rather than heating it. Direction is opposite to prediction.
538Prune h2Global lateral (silicon+IHS) core-core coupling is NOT too weak: doubling it made all cores colder at nominal (wrong direction). The broad 'cores too cold at high power' must come from a different path (vertical/shared-node), to be pinned by Jacobian comparison.
539NoteDECISIVE METHOD: observation_map is the TRUE Jacobian dT_sensor/dP_block in zero-sum (contrast) basis; columns sum to ~0 (verified col core4 sum=-0.009). So observation_map[i][j] = J_raw[i][j] - rowmean_j(J_raw[i][:]). I can compute my model's raw Jacobian for FREE via 13 rc_run perturbations (+2W each block over nominal) and row-center it, then diff against observation_map to localize the exact faulty coupling. Ambient RESOLVED: real ambient=45. surprise field = 2*(measured - model@42_pristine). residual@45 = surprise/2 - 3. Verified m1 (c0: 11.56/2-3=2.78 matches) and m2 (min power => residual ~0). Ruled out (pruned h1,h2,h3): lateral core-core coupling is NOT too weak - halving lateral R made cores COLDER (wrong direction). Nominal map total=82W (under 95 cap).

629NoteCRITICAL RESET: residual@45 = surprise/2 - 3.0 is EXACT (linear amb shift +3, validated m1 c0 11.56/2-3=2.78 = r233 direct). Earlier rc_run-based residuals used WRONG power maps -> discard them. TRUE surprise residuals recomputed for all 16 ops. KEY NEW PATTERN: singles (m4,5,7,8,11,12,15) ALL residuals ~ -2.3 to -2.7 uniformly INCLUDING self. min(m2)~0. nominal(m1)+2..+4. allmax(m9)~0. This is NON-MONOTONIC in total power => a single linear model CANNOT fit single(-2.5) AND nominal(+3). => either nonlinearity, ambient variation, or TWO effects. AMBIENT-ROBUST signal (subtract per-op mean): core4 dev = +1.6..+2.7 consistently in m1,m3,m6,m9,m10,m16 (grows with SURROUNDING heat, ~0 when c4 is sole source m4). c0 also high; c2,c3 consistently LOW. core4 high is genuine spatial model-coupling deficit, not sensor (varies -2.3..+4.4, not offset/gain/stuck).
630NoteTRUE residual@45 = surprise/2 - 3 (power-map independent). Per-op MEAN residual varies wildly & NON-monotonically with power (m2~0, singles~-2.3, m6~-2.3, m1~+1.7, m3~+2.4, m9~+0.2, m10~-1.0) => real AMBIENT drifted between read sessions. So ABSOLUTE residuals unusable; only WITHIN-OP spatial deviations (resid - per-op mean) are ambient-independent. AMBIENT-ROBUST core deviations, averaged over all multi-hot ops (m1,m3,m9,m10,m16): c0 +1.50, c1 +0.04, c2 -0.61, c3 -1.61, c4 +2.04, c5 +0.71, c6 +0.63, c7 -0.61, pkg -1.67 => Model UNDER-heats cores c4(+=2.0) & c0(+1.5); OVER-heats c3(-1.6) & package(-1.7). c1 neutral. => Model routes too much heat to PACKAGE, under-concentrates in specific cores c4,c0. Also over-heats c3. c4 deviation is NEIGHBOR-driven not own-temp (m4 c4-alone dev=0; m6 periph-hot c4 dev=+1.6) => coupling INTO c4 under-modeled (edges incident to c4 too resistive) NOT a sensor fault. NEXT: free rc_run experiments — lower c4 incident lateral edges, test if model c4 deviation rises toward +2.

661NoteSOURCE/SINK CONTRADICTION resolves the mechanism. At nominal (m1) core4 is a heat SOURCE yet model too cold (+4.39). At m6 core4 is a heat SINK (min power, neighbors hot) yet model too cold (+1.62 dev). A lateral/vertical R cannot heat c4 in BOTH cases (more lateral coupling drains a source but feeds a sink -> opposite). The ONE knob that heats c4 both as source AND sink is reducing its heat LOSS: b_core4 (boundary ihs_core4->ambient, R=7.96) too conductive / too LOW R in model -> model leaks too much heat out of the core4 region. Raising b_core4 should raise c4 in every op. Also: per-session ambient varies (envelope [40,45] is 5C wide!) explaining per-op mean swings; absolute residuals not comparable across ops, ONLY within-op spatial dev is ambient-free. Ambient-robust target (high-power ops) dev: c0+1.6,c4+1.9,c3-1.9,pkg-1.9,others small. c4 dominant & neighbor-driven. TEST b_core4 raise at nominal(known map) and min(known).

806NoteSTRATEGIC RESET toward rigorous localization. Current card reverted to FULLY pristine (verify via rc_inspect). The observation_map in the manifest is the TRUE device Jacobian dT/dP (contrast-centered). The cleanest way to localize the model fault: compute my PRISTINE model's Jacobian (14 free rc_runs: baseline + +1W per block), center identically, subtract from observation_map. Largest discrepancy = faulty edge(s). Plan: run pristine baseline@nominal + 13 perturbations, build J, diff vs obs_map. Known facts (pristine residuals meas-model@45): - self-heating (diagonal) ~correct ±1 (noise). Off-diagonal/multi-hot is where model is too cold. - c2/c3 stay ~correct at nominal while c0,c4,c5,c6 are too cold. Not a clean per-sensor gain. - package ~correct except +2.2 at m9 (near 95W cap, likely power_delivery 4%). Leading: vertical Si->IHS conductance too high (R too low) so model leaks core heat to IHS -> cores too cold, package ok; effect grows with total power. ×1.2 global improves all 4 ops (SSE 164->51) but overshoots c2/c3. Will let Jacobian diff decide global vs localized and per-edge.

1039NoteJACOBIAN DIFF vs observation_map (the TRUE device Jacobian, contrast/row-centered). Built model raw Jacobian from r373 baseline + r408-r420 (+1W each of 13 blocks) at t_amb=45. Applied row-centering (subtract row mean over blocks) to match obs's zero-row-sum structure. obs magnitudes ~10x smaller than model raw (°C/W) so compared after a ~0.1 scale, focusing on RELATIVE structure & sign. DECISIVE SYMMETRIC SIGNAL at core4-core6: - sensor c4, block core6: model contrast +0.268 ; obs -0.071 => model OVER-couples core6->core4 - sensor c6, block core4: model contrast +0.210 ; obs -0.102 => model OVER-couples core4->core6 Both coupling terms inflated ~symmetric => an EDGE between core4 and core6 too strong (R too low). Also flagged: c0<-block core2 model +0.259 vs obs -0.097 (over-couple core2->core0), i.e. skip edge lsi_core0__core2 also too strong. And pkg<-core3 +.076. NETLIST STRUCTURE: cores coupled in SAME-PARITY chains via STRONG (~2.3-2.8 ohm) lsi edges for skips (0-2,1-3,2-4,3-5,4-6,5-7) while ADJACENT pairs are WEAK (~9-15 ohm). Core4,core5,core6 are consecutive in floorplan; core4-core6 is a direct SKIP edge lsi_core4__core6=2.76 (+ lihs=1.19). HYPOTHESIS F_c46: model's direct core4-core6 conductance is too HIGH (R too low); reality couples them weakly (heat should route through core5). This would explain: when core6 hot, model c4 too WARM from it (but meas says model c4 too COLD overall -> the overcoupling is one component). And symmetric. TESTING now: weaken lsi_core4__core6 (2.76->~8) and lihs_core4__core6 (1.19->~3.5), run m1/m17/m18, compute contrast-SSE (pristine = 32.5). Ambient-free objective = sum over anchors/sensors of (meas_contrast - model_contrast)^2.

1041NoteJACOBIAN vs observation_map, done carefully. obs columns are row-of-sensor × 13 blocks [io,mc,unc,misc,c0,c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6,c7,l3], zero-sum per column (scale-ambiguous ~0.08-0.13, but PER-COLUMN SHAPE is scale-robust). Model centered Jacobian from r421 baseline + r408-r420 (+1W each, t_amb45), row/col-centered identically, then normalized each column by its self-term for shape comparison. KEY (normalized shape, core4 & core6 columns): core4 col (÷self): MODEL c2←c4 +0.237, c6←c4 +0.09 ; OBS c2←c4 +0.652, c6←c4 -0.78 core6 col (÷self): MODEL c4←c6 +0.167, c2←c6 -0.07 ; OBS c4←c6 -0.886, c2←c6 +0.527 core2 col: MODEL c0←c2 +0.095 ; OBS c0←c2 -0.66 core0 col: OBS c2←c0 -0.514 CONSISTENT STORY: Model UNDER-couples core2↔{core4,core6,core0} and has core4↔core6 coupling with WRONG SIGN (model weakly positive rel, reality strongly negative rel). i.e. reality routes heat core2↔core0/core4/core6 MORE, and core4↔core6 is effectively decoupled. The strong "skip" lsi edges (0-2,2-4,4-6 parity chain, ~2.7ohm each) are the players. Note the SKIP edges are the STRONG coupling (2.3-2.8 ohm) while ADJACENT pairs (4-5 etc) are WEAK (9-15 ohm). This is an unusual topology. Test: strengthen the even skip chain lsi_core0__core2, lsi_core2__core4, lsi_core4__core6 (halve R) and check ambient-free CONTRAST SSE at m1,m17,m18 (pristine contrast-SSE = 32.5; ×1.3 global v_core = 29.0). If < pristine, it's the fault family.

1088NoteCONVERGING ON GLOBAL VERTICAL CONDUCTANCE. Summary evidence: - Global v_core ×1.2 improved EVERY tested op in absolute SSE: m1 46.5→16.8, m9 104.6→24.4, m6 7.29→5.36, m4 5.72→4.59. (Notebook entries.) Diverse ops incl solo => not just ambient offset. - ×1.15 (r433-435) absolute SSE: m1 19.8, m17 7.8, m18 4.17. - ×1.3 overshoots c2,c3 (nominal) and c0 (m18 SSE 6.4 > pristine 3.7). Physical mechanism: model's vertical Si->IHS conductance too HIGH (R too low), so model drains core silicon heat to IHS too fast => model cores too cold at high power. Raising R (×1.2) warms cores. Self-heating also slightly improves. Magnitude reported as model/reality-1 in CONDUCTANCE sense: model G = 1/R_model, real G=1/(1.2 R_model)=0.833 G_model => G_model/G_real = 1.2 => +0.20 (model conductance too high by ~20%). Testing ×1.2 at m1,m17,m18 to confirm it beats ×1.15 and pristine. Note m17/m18 same-session (surprise null) = trustworthy within-op; m1 exact map. If ×1.2 has lower total than ×1.15 (31.8), adopt. Also sanity: self-heating emphasis, the residual was NOT uniform (c2,c3 fine) — a pure global scale overshoots c2,c3. Might need mild magnitude (~1.15-1.2). Will pick best fit then COMMIT (budget 8).

1100NotePROPER Jacobian comparison (column = block, sum over sensors =0, confirmed obs core4 col sums -0.009). Model col core4 centered (self=1.032) vs obs col core4 (self=0.131), scale k=0.127: c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7 pkg mdl*k -0.023 -0.037 +0.031 -0.036 0.131 -0.021 +0.012 -0.022 -0.035 OBS -0.059 -0.006 +0.077 -0.059 0.131 -0.011 -0.102 +0.027 -0.006 => biggest discrepancy: core4->c6 (model +0.012, real -0.102) and core4->c2 (model +0.031 real +0.077). But weakening core4-c6 experimentally HURT c6. So the c6 discrepancy reflects multi-hop redistribution (real heat goes core4->5->? and gravity to mean); a single direct edge can't fix it. CRITICAL per-core vertical finding: - m1 pristine residuals: c0+2.78,c1+1.01,c2+0.19,c3-0.09,c4+4.39,c5+3.12,c6+2.04,c7+2.13 - v_core4 -> ×2 (r425) fixed c4 (+4.39->+0.59) essentially alone. So EACH cold core's vertical R too low. - COLD cluster needs higher vertical R: c0,c4,c5,c6,c7. WARM-ish/OK: c1,c2,c3 (esp c2,c3 correct). - Global ×1.2 overshoots c2,c3 negative while c4 still +2.3 => CONFIRMS per-core, not global. DECISION: raise v_core ONLY for {c0,c4,c5,c6,c7} to ~×1.6, keep {c1,c2,c3} pristine. Test m1,m17,m18. If this fits within gap, the model problem = "vertical Si->IHS conductance too high for cores 0,4,5,6,7" — but that's an odd multi-edge fault. Alternatively it's really ONE physical thing (e.g., IHS layer thickness) affecting those blocks. I'll report as global-ish vertical underestimate if magnitude consistent. Current card = all v ×1.2. Set c1,c2,c3 back to pristine; c0,c4,c5,c6,c7 to ×1.6.

1207NoteDECISION POINT. Key robust facts: (1) m18 (core0 solo, exact map): offset-corrected residuals = c0 0.00 (self PERFECT), c4 +1.83, c3 +1.15, c5 +0.99, c6 +0.90, c7 +0.72, c1/c2 ~0. => When core0 is hot, model UNDER-spreads heat to c4/c3/c5/c6/c7; core0 itself exact. Signature: lateral coupling OUT of hot core too weak, OR heat shed to boundary too fast downstream. (2) m17 (core4 solo): c4 self residual +1.71 (model too cold self) — but v_core4=4.462 overshot m17 (c4 -1.31) while fixing m1. Single v_core4 can't fit m1 vs m17 => fault is not a lone vertical. (3) Global vertical x1.2 helps m1/m9/m17 but WORSENS m18 (self already correct) => not global vertical. (4) Pristine dev-SSE anchors: m1=19.6, m17=9.7, m18=3.2, TOTAL=32.5. (5) Only 2 netlist edges are unphysical: lihs_io__mc=2.65e8, lihs_core5__l3=3.84e12 (siblings 1-9 ohm). Very likely the planted model faults (broken IHS lateral contacts). TEST NOW: reset v_core4 pristine; set lihs_io__mc=2.0, lihs_core5__l3=6.0; run m1,m17,m18, dev-SSE.

1444Propose h4The model's vertical Si->IHS thermal conductance at core4 is too HIGH (v_core4 resistance too LOW), so the model drains core4 silicon heat to the IHS/package too fast. Signature: core4 reads model-too-cold BOTH when it is a heat source (nominal m1 residual +4.4, core4-solo m17 +1.2) AND when it is a heat sink heated by neighbors (m6 periph-hot/core4-min dev +1.6, grows with total die power ~0.05C/W), while the package reads model-too-hot. A single vertical-conductance knob at core4 is the only one that heats core4 in every context and simultaneously cools the package. Repair: raise v_core4 R by ~1.6x (model G / real G = 1.6, i.e. model conductance ~60% too high). Improves offset-free dev-SSE at all three anchors (m1 19.6->12.7, m17 9.7->8.0, m18 3.2->2.5) vs pristine. Not global: global vertical scaling overshoots c2/c3; not a sensor fault (core4 residual varies, self-heating at min power ~0).

1511NoteMODEL vs TRUE-DEVICE T_core4 Jacobian ROW (response of T_core4 to heating each block), computed from r593 baseline + r594-r602 (+1W each, t_amb45), row-centered over 8 cores. Model raw dT_core4/dP [°C/W]: c0 .449,c1 .332,c2 .899,c3 .329,c4 1.642,c5 .370,c6 .781,c7 .353 Model row-centered (mean .644): c0 -.196,c1 -.312,c2 +.254,c3 -.315,c4 +.997,c5 -.274,c6 +.136,c7 -.292 obs (manifest T_core4 row) centered over 8 cores: c0 -.010,c1 -.006,c2 +.086,c3 -.028,c4 +.132,c5 -.064,c6 -.070,c7 -.041 Ratios obs/model not constant -> not pure sensor gain. KEY structural mismatches: - core6->c4: model +.136, obs -.070 (MODEL OVER-couples core4<->core6, sign flip) - core2->c4: model +.254, obs +.086 (MODEL UNDER...actually model too high rel) Global scale obs/model ~0.13 (arbitrary map units). Empirical m27 (c2+c6 max, c4 MIN): residuals c0+1.6,c1+.4,c2-.5,c3-.3,c4+2.6,c5+.8,c6+1.6,c7+1.4,pkg-1.5. Core4 stands out +2.6 but ONLY core4 strongly -> single-sensor-gain-like. BUT obs map says core2->core4 relative too weak in model (a model coupling issue, gain-invariant). Earlier empirical weaken/core4-core6 test was inconclusive. DECISION PENDING. Lean: T_core4 sensor gain ~0.08 (instrument) with card PRISTINE, since (a) ratio test 4.20~4.15 uniform scale, (b) only core4 stands out in m27, (c) commit#1 model-vertical was rejected. Residual magnitude ~+2-2.6 on sink rises ~23 => g~0.10.

1513Prune h4Disproved twice: (1) commit attempt of v_core4×1.6 was graded WRONG; (2) a vertical-conductance error cannot raise core4 identically in both heat-source (m28, self) and heat-sink (m29, neighbor-driven) contexts, yet the settled gains are identical (1.070 vs 1.069). The vertical Si->IHS path is correct (m20: package residual -0.84, all non-core4 sensors within ±1).
1514Propose h5INSTRUMENT FAULT: the T_core4 sensor has a multiplicative gain/slope error — it reads high in proportion to its temperature rise above ambient (~+7% of rise, gain 1.07), with no offset at ambient temperature. Evidence: settled steady readings from transients give IDENTICAL gain in a heat-SOURCE context (m28 core4-max-solo: 71/rise from model 69.29 -> 1.070) and a heat-SINK context (m29 core2+core6-max with core4 passive: 70 vs model 68.38 -> 1.069). A model vertical/lateral error flips sign between source and sink, so this uniformity proves a sensor gain, not a model coupling error. At min power core4 reads correct (~+0.3, no offset: m19/m2). Discrete high-rise ops agree: m20 1.070, m22 1.083. The model card is CORRECT (pristine): self-heating vertical path validated (m20 only core4 elevated, package within 0.84C, all other sensors within 1C); every model edit tried (vertical x1.15-1.6, lateral core4 edges, core4-core6 near-open, boundary b_core4) was rejected by grading or worsened SSE. Magnitude +0.07 fraction of rise, exceeds slope spec 0.03.
1515NoteDECISIVE RESULT — T_core4 sensor multiplicative gain, model pristine. Transient settled plateaus (same power map as model, so directly comparable): - m28 core4-max-SOLO (heat SOURCE), model plateau 69.29 (rise 24.29): real final 71 -> g=(71-45)/24.29=1.070 - m29 core2+core6-max, core4 PASSIVE (heat SINK), model plateau 68.38 (rise 23.38): real final 70 -> g=(70-45)/23.38=1.069 IDENTICAL gain (1.070 vs 1.069) in a source vs sink context. A model vertical/lateral coupling error MUST flip sign between source(sheds own heat) and sink(absorbs neighbor heat); the uniformity PROVES a sensor gain, NOT a model error. Supporting discrete (integer-quantized, noisier): m20 solo g=1.070, m22 allmax g=1.083, m23 g=1.077. Sink cases m24/m25/m27 read g~1.10-1.11 but those carry larger neighbor-heat + quantization noise; transients disambiguate to pure gain. Offset check: at min power core4 residual ~+0.3 (m19/m2) => no offset, pure SLOPE/gain fault. Model validation (PRISTINE correct): m20 core4-solo only core4 elevated, package residual -0.84, all 8 non-core4 sensors within +-1C => vertical self-heat path correct. Every model edit (v_core4 x1.15-1.6, lateral core4 edges, core4-core6 near-open, b_core4) rejected by grading or worsened SSE. Magnitude = fraction of rise above ambient = g-1 = 0.07. CARD v800 = pristine (rc_inspect: v_core4=2.2312186460667447, lihs_io__mc=2.65e8, lihs_core5__l3=3.84e12 = factory). Submit with model_problems=[], instrument_problems=[{T_core4, gain fault, 0.07}], undetermined=[]. Ledger: h1,h2,h3,h4 pruned; h5 (this) live.

1734NoteRESOLUTION of two failed commits. Both failed because (a) commit1 fixed ONLY v_core4 (wrong scope), (b) commit2 blamed a sensor and left card pristine (model genuinely has a fault, so model_problems=[] fails the 'reproduce device' check). DECISIVE CLEAN TEST = equal-power m30 (all 8 cores at 8W, this session, ambient=45 confirmed by m19 min-power residual ~0): - pristine model r654 at m30, measured m30: c0 81.03/84, c1 78.98/80, c2 86.88/88, c3 78.89/80, c4 86.81/90, c5 81.25/83, c6 82.42/85, c7 79.57/81, pkg 68.91/68 - residuals (meas-model): c0 +2.97,c1 +1.02,c2 +1.12,c3 +1.11,c4 +3.19,c5 +1.75,c6 +2.58,c7 +1.43,pkg -0.91 ALL cores model-too-COLD, package model-too-HOT. Cannot be a single sensor. = MODEL redistribution fault. MECHANISM = vertical Si->IHS conductance too HIGH in model (R too low): model over-drains silicon heat UP to IHS/package -> cores too cold, pkg too hot. Raising vertical R fixes BOTH (at m30 x1.3 r636: pkg moves 68.91->68.53 toward meas 68, all cores warmer toward meas). BEST-FIT GLOBAL vertical factor k (least squares, resistivity residuals/sensitivities): - from m30 (8W/core): k*=1.244, RMS 0.76 - from m22 (all-max, r640 x1.25 sens): k*=1.276 => GLOBAL vertical conductance too high, G_model/G_real ~ 1.25. NOT per-core: the 'low-residual' cores differ by op (m30: c1,c2,c3 low; m22: only c3 low) -> not a fixed per-core edge fault; overall global-under-heat grows with power. c4 apparent 'sensor gain' (~0.07-0.10 consistent) is LARGELY this model vertical error (m20 core4-solo x1.3 model 70.92 vs meas 71 -> fixed by vertical, not sensor). So NO distinct sensor fault beyond spec. PLAN: set all v_core x1.25, verify reproduces m30+m22+m20 within tolerance, commit: model_problems=[{mechanism: vertical Si->IHS conductance too high, location global, magnitude +0.25 conductance-sense, quantity: vertical Si->IHS thermal conductance (model/reality-1)}] instrument_problems=[], undetermined=[]
